data.title: Basis steady while farmer selling stays quiet
data.description:
Spot basis bids for hard red winter wheat were unchanged in the southern US Plains on Friday while farmer grain sales were quiet, merchandisers said.

  • Cash trading was subdued after futures markets closed on Thursday for the US Thanksgiving holiday.

  • On Monday, the US Department of Agriculture is scheduled to issue a weekly update on condition ratings for the US winter wheat crop.

  • US hard red winter wheat export sales for 2026-27 were 172,277 metric tons in the week that ended on November 19, the USDA said.

  • Total weekly US wheat export sales were 564,683 metric tons, above analysts' expectations of 250,000 to 550,000 metric tons.

  • K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) futures were 9 cents higher at $6.13 per bushel in afternoon trading. The contract rebounded after falling on Wednesday to its lowest level since February 17 at $5.97-1/2 a bushel.

data.title: Synthetic share repurchases in SmartCraft Group AB
data.description:
27 November 2026 – SmartCraft Group AB (publ) (“SmartCraft” or the “Company”) has, between 23 November 2026 and 27 November 2026, carried out synthetic repurchases of a total of 508,000 ordinary shares under the synthetic share buyback programme resolved upon by the Board of Directors.

On 5 November 2026, SmartCraft announced that the Board of Directors, pursuant to the authorisation granted by the Extraordinary General Meeting held on 29 April 2026, had resolved to initiate a synthetic share buyback programme and enter into an agreement with DNB Carnegie Investment Bank AB (publ) (“DNB Carnegie”) to enable synthetic repurchases of SmartCraft’s ordinary shares on Nasdaq Stockholm. The programme covers synthetic repurchases for an aggregate amount of up to SEK 120 million and a maximum of 6,990,277 ordinary shares. The purpose of the programme is to enable SmartCraft to continuously adjust its capital structure and thereby contribute to increased shareholder value.

data.title: Nvidia Faces Short-Term Washington Volatility, but AI Growth Story Holds Firm — Market Talk
data.description: Nvidia's multi-year AI growth thesis remains intact even as CEO Jensen Huang prepares to testify on Capitol Hill next week, Yorkville Ives's Dan Ives says. While Ives expects some short-term volatility ahead of Huang's congressional hearings, he maintains an outperform rating and a $250 price target on the stock. Ives dismisses recent bear arguments centered on regulatory scrutiny and Chinese export loopholes, estimating those sales represent "a containable 15% to 20% of revenue at most" and aren't factored into 4Q guidance. Even if 20% of planned data centers aren't built and Asia loophole sales disappear entirely, "we are still bullish on the thesis into the next two to three years," Ives writes, noting Huang "carries the weight of the entire tech sector and AI Revolution." (adriano.marchese@wsj.com)

data.title: Chile's Codelco swings to $1.4 billion nine-month loss after asset writedowns
data.description:
Chile's Codelco, one of the world's largest copper producers, on Friday reported a pre-tax loss of $1.4 billion for the first nine months of 2026, driven largely by asset impairment charges totaling $4.82 billion across three key mining divisions.

The state-owned miner's own copper production totaled 853,000 metric tons in the January-September period, down from the 937,000 tons reported a year earlier.

Codelco said it reduced the accounting value of three major divisions - Chuquicamata, Salvador and Gabriela Mistral - to reflect lower expected future profitability.

Earlier this month, Codelco lowered its production guidance for 2026 to slightly over 1.2 million metric tons, down from a previous target of 1.34 million tons.

The results come as Chief Executive Jorge Gomez, who took over earlier this year, seeks to reverse years of production declines while dealing with the fallout from a widespread misreporting case.

Codelco said it had overstated copper output by 42,100 metric tons in 2024 and 2025. The misreporting spanned multiple mines over the two-year period.

Chairman Bernardo Fontaine said at an extraordinary shareholder's meeting on November 5 that the impact from a portion of the improperly reported copper was equivalent to between $120 million and $140 million. A Codelco statement showed that financial loss corresponded to 15,200 metric tons of copper, part of the total over-reported amount.

Codelco's copper production is critical to global supply. But the company has been beset by debt, budget overruns, production challenges and fatal accidents and its output sank to two-decade lows in 2022 and 2023.

Meanwhile global demand for copper has been high and is expected to continue rising due to electrification, power grids, electric vehicles and AI data centers.

Fontaine, who was appointed this year by President Jose Antonio Kast's new government, said in November that output over the next four years would be around 1.3 million metric tons a year.

data.title: Quality Power Raises ₹570 crore through QIP, allots 39 lakh shares at ₹1,459 each
data.description:
Quality Power Electrical Equipments Ltd on Friday (November 27) said it has closed its qualified institutional placement (QIP) at an issue price of ₹1,458.76 per share, allocating 39,07,431 equity shares to eligible qualified institutional buyers.

The issue price includes a premium of ₹1,448.76 per share and a 5% discount of ₹76.77 per share to the floor price of ₹1,535.53, the company said in a regulatory filing.

The company's Fund Raising Committee approved the closure of the issue after receiving application forms and funds in the escrow account from eligible qualified institutional buyers, in accordance with the terms of the issue.

The committee also approved and adopted the placement document dated November 27, 2026, and finalised the confirmation of allocation note to be sent to eligible investors, informing them of their share allotment.

Shares of Quality Power Electrical Equipments Ltd ended at ₹1,495.00, up by ₹22.55, or 1.53%, on the BSE.

data.title: European shares log strong weekly gains; markets await Spanish election
data.description:
Key points:
  • STOXX 600 set for weekly gains in broad-based rally
  • Spanish election to be in focus this weekend
  • ASML, Infineon lead semiconductor stocks advances
  • Thales in talks to buy controlling Lumibird stake

By Anjana Jayakrishnan Nair and Johann M Cherian

Europe's benchmark share index closed at a one-week high on Friday after broad sectoral gains as investors bought riskier assets following steep losses earlier this month.

Investors' attention now turns to Spain's election on Sunday.

The pan-European STOXX 600 gained 1% to 643.85 points. It gained nearly 3% on the week, its sharpest weekly rise since mid-May, bouncing back from the steepest weekly decline since late March 2025.

"There doesn't seem to be any firm catalyst behind the bounce that we've seen, but it has been a very bruising month. What we're seeing here is dip buyers coming in," said Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at StoneX.

Equities were rebounding from what has been a bruising month for AI-exposed global stocks as investors grew frustrated with returns on debt-backed AI investments and a brief leadership crisis at chip giant Nvidia .

On Friday, however, European technology stocks (.SX8P) added 2%, led by semiconductor shares ASML , ASM International and Infineon , which gained between 2% and 2.7%. For the week, the index was 1% higher.

Mining stocks (.SXPP) jumped more than 3.5% as copper and gold prices rose. Fresnillo and Pan African Resources rose more than 4% each.

Defence stocks also gained, with Rheinmetall up 3.3% after a report on a planned AI-platform partnership with Deutsche Telekom.

The broader aerospace and defence index (.SXPARO) climbed 2% after Bloomberg News reported the European Union was planning new funds to replace US war-fighting capabilities.

The spotlight will now be on Sunday's snap election in Spain, called by Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez after parliament rejected housing measures aimed at tackling a crisis that has triggered protests across the country.

Alberto Nunez Feijoo's centre-right People's Party (PP) is leading in polls ahead of the vote, although most suggest he will have to form a coalition with far-right Vox to secure a parliamentary majority.

The vote could be a gauge of public sentiment ahead of pivotal elections in France and Italy that also witnessed similar protests, at a time when investors are sensitive to the massive debt pile of developed economies.

"With fiscal policy set to be tightened again and uncertainty likely to spike around the presidential elections, growth will probably be very weak again in 2027," Andrew Kenningham, chief Europe economist at Capital Economics said on France.

Investors, meanwhile, shrugged off the Trump administration's move to propose tariffs on goods from the EU.

Consumer-facing foods and beverages (.SX3P) slipped 0.3%, with sportswear makers Adidas and Puma flat and down about 1%, respectively.

Data this week showed US inflation rose further last month, and the economy grew more than previously expected, adding to bets on interest rate hikes.

Among others, Thales gained 2.3% after French laser technology company Lumibird said it had entered exclusive talks to sell a controlling stake to the defence group. Lumibird surged 18.1%.

data.title: Abu Dhabi Equities Could Offer Gulf's Best Risk-Adjusted Returns — Market Talk
data.description: Abu Dhabi equities are expected to offer the highest risk-adjusted returns among Gulf markets in 2027, Bahrain-based investment bank SICO says. Banks should benefit from sustained borrowing demand from companies and government-related entities, while higher crude production could support government spending. However, banking valuations could become a challenge following a roughly 20% rally in the sector this year. SICO also favors Abu Dhabi's real estate over Dubai's, citing a more limited supply pipeline and growing interest from international investors. A resolution to the regional conflict could further support property and tourism stocks. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

data.title: Pegasystems, Appian strike eve-of-trial settlement in defamation case
data.description:
By Nate Raymond

Software company Pegasystems has settled a defamation lawsuit accusing rival Appian of making misleading statements after winning a $2 billion trade secrets verdict against Pegasystems that was later overturned on appeal.

The companies said in a joint filing in Boston federal court on Wednesday that they had reached a settlement on the eve of a trial that was set to begin on Monday to resolve Pegasystems' claims and Appian's allegations of false advertising against Pegasystems.

An Appian spokesperson in a statement called the terms of the settlement confidential. The related trade secrets case in Virginia has not settled and remains set for a retrial on January 11, the spokesperson added.

Pegasystems in the Massachusetts case had sought $41.7 million in damages, while Appian had been seeking to force its rival to disgorge $109.5 million in profits and pay it $31.8 million in lost profits.

Pegasystems had no immediate comment on Friday.

The case arose from a separate trade secrets lawsuit that Virginia-based Appian filed in 2020 against Massachusetts-based Pegasystems in Virginia state court.

Appian alleged that Pegasystems hired a contractor to steal confidential information from Appian's software platform in order to improve its products and better train its sales force. A jury in 2022 awarded Appian $2.04 billion in damages, but the award was overturned on appeal. A retrial is set for January.

Pegasystems filed the federal case against Appian in 2023, alleging that after the verdict Appian made defamatory and misleading statements in social media advertisements, presentations and a press release concerning the company.

Pegasystems said those statements suggested that the company had been found guilty of a crime, that the verdict put its viability into question, and that founder and CEO Alan Trefler had used aliases to gain improper access to Appian’s software.

The company brought claims for defamation, trade libel and false advertising under the Lanham Act.

Appian denied the allegations and asserted counterclaims.

US District Judge Leo Sorokin in August dismissed many of those counterclaims and an effort to force Pegasystems to disgorge $2.33 billion in profits it earned from 2022 to 2025. But he allowed Appian to proceed to trial on certain counterclaims brought under the Lanham Act.

Appian alleged that Pegasystems made misleading statements, including ones that suggested a single employee was primarily responsible for the conduct at issue in the Virginia case and that the company could comfortably absorb the $2 billion judgment. Pegasystems denied the allegations.

The case is Pegasystems Inc v Appian Corporation, US District Court for the District of Massachusetts, No. 23-cv-11776.

For Pegasystems: R. David Hosp of Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe

For Appian: Adeel Mangi of Linklaters
